title: Netflix Launches NextGen Writers' Program to Discover India's New Storytellers
excerpt: The streaming giant is bringing its global talent development initiative to India for the first time, offering early-career writers the chance to develop original series concepts with mentorship from industry professionals.
body:
• Netflix has launched the NextGen India Writers' Program, its first talent development initiative for writers in India, accepting applications until September 1, 2026.
  • India is the third country after France and the Netherlands to host the program, which targets writers with a maximum of three years of professional screenwriting experience.
  • Selected writers will participate in a week-long simulated writers' room workshop, followed by six weeks of mentored development, culminating in a pitch to Netflix India's content team.

Netflix has unveiled the NextGen India Writers' Program, bringing its global talent development initiative to the country for the first time as it looks to identify and nurture the next generation of Indian screenwriters. Applications are open through September 1.

India is the third market, after France and the Netherlands, to host the program — a signal of the growing global appetite for Indian stories and the streaming platform's deepening investment in the country's creative ecosystem.

How the Program Works

The initiative targets early-career writers with a maximum of three years of professional screenwriting experience. Selected participants will enter a two-month hybrid program that includes mentorship, workshops, and hands-on support from industry experts.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=kr83QDHa_KY

The centrepiece is a week-long workshop described as a "simulated writers' room," where participants will learn from industry professionals how to pitch and break a story. This is followed by six weeks of online sessions with mentors and peers, during which writers will develop detailed pitches for original series concepts.

The program culminates with participants pitching their ideas directly to Netflix India's content team. The instructor roster includes screenwriter Barbara Nance, known for her work in television. Selected applicants will be announced on December 15, with the workshop expected to begin in February 2027.

"Every great story begins with a writer. In a country as creatively rich and diverse as India, we know there are countless people with extraordinary stories to tell who simply haven't had the opportunity yet."

— Monika Shergill, Vice President, Content, Netflix India

Building on Indian Content Investment

The NextGen program builds on Netflix India's track record of backing emerging creators. The company pointed to projects such as The Railway Men, created by first-time showrunner Shiv Rawail, and The Bastards of Bollywood, the directorial debut of Aryan Khan, as examples of its commitment to new voices.

Netflix also highlighted Operation Safed Sagar, an upcoming original series developed by first-time creators Abhijeet Singh Parmar, Kushal Srivastava, Oni Sen, and Mehboob Pal Singh Brar.

The move comes alongside other Netflix India creative initiatives. Earlier this year, the company partnered with Pluc.tv to launch a Climate Scriptwriting Lab, which supported 60 writers across Indian languages in developing environmentally themed fiction screenplays. That initiative included mentorship from established writers such as Sumit Roy, Saiwyn Quadras, and Akshat Verma.

A Wider Streaming Battle

The writers' program arrives as competition among streaming platforms for Indian content intensifies. Amazon Prime Video, Disney+ Hotstar, and JioCinema have all expanded their original slates in India, while domestic platforms like Zee5 and SonyLIV continue to invest in regional-language content.

Indian stories have found growing international audiences in recent years, with Netflix titles reaching viewers across South Asia, the Middle East, and diaspora markets worldwide. The platform's investment in early-stage talent reflects a long-term bet on the depth of India's creative pipeline rather than simply licensing existing intellectual property.

"We believe the next chapter of Indian entertainment will be shaped by bold new storytellers with fresh perspectives and distinctive voices," Shergill said. "Because the next great Indian story could come from anywhere, and we can't wait to discover it."

By the end of the program, selected writers will have developed their original series concepts into professionally structured series bibles — a document that maps out characters, story arcs, and episode breakdowns, serving as the blueprint for a potential Netflix production.
nri_angle: For Indian diaspora creators interested in screenwriting, the program represents a direct pathway into one of the world's largest streaming platforms, with applications open globally until September 1.
